clue.text: Hazard to shipping? Calls in distress around end of 22 January

indicators.note: around tells us the rearranged letters wrap round the next piece
something in distress is in disorder, so the letters of calls are thrown into a new order
end of picks out only the final letter of the word January

explanation.surface: A coastguard notes distress calls coming in at the end of the month about a danger to ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in distress' rearranges CALLS to SCLLA; 'around' puts it round Y, the 'end of' January. Scylla was the sea monster opposite Charybdis in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend the monster on a rock beside a narrow strait devoured sailors from passing vessels, a peril to every passing boat.

clue.text: Conservative dodge to exclude women -it's a twist

indicators.note: to exclude means one piece is left out of the other

parts.note: a wrinkle is a clever trick or dodge

explanation.surface: A Tory ruse to keep women out is a turn of events.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'wrinkle' is an informal word for a clever trick; 'to exclude' takes out its W.
explanation.definitionFit: To crumple or crease something, giving it a fold or curl.

clue.text: A weaving machine is to come into view

definitions.meaning: to appear, often in a threatening way

explanation.definitionFit: It is both the apparatus on which textiles are woven and a verb for appearing large and threatening.

clue.text: Tree people respected citizens

parts.note: the alder is a tree of the birch family
men are people

explanation.surface: People of standing in town gather under a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Aldermen were senior members of a borough or county council in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior councillors or elected officials of a town are civic figures of standing.

clue.text: Good Dickens character 23 showing resentful attitude 25

parts.note: Barnaby Rudge is the title hero of a Dickens novel

explanation.surface: A virtuous figure from Dickens turns out to be bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnaby Rudge is the title of a Charles Dickens novel and the name of its hero.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-held feeling of ill will over a past wrong is exactly a resentful attitude.

clue.text: Man shows energy in the garden

indicators.note: in places the one letter inside the garden word

parts.note: a garth is an enclosed garden or courtyard
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A gardener displays his vigour among the flower beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts E inside GARTH, an old word for an enclosed garden.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common Welsh male name, so it stands for a man.

clue.text: In a trice nun could be lacking in confidence

indicators.note: could be says these letters might be rearranged to form another word

explanation.surface: A nun who suddenly doubts her faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges A TRICE NUN; 'In' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unsure or doubtful means lacking self-assurance.

clue.text: Old song about awful con in site of massacre

indicators.note: about tells us the song goes around the shuffled letters

parts.note: a glee is an old part-song for unaccompanied voices

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters are in a terrible mess

explanation.surface: An old ballad tells of a dreadful trick at a place of slaughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' signals the anagram and 'about' the container. The 1692 massacre of the MacDonalds took place in this Scottish glen.
explanation.definitionFit: In 1692 the Scottish glen saw the slaughter of members of Clan MacDonald.

clue.text: Request for armour 26 bought and brought to your door

definitions.text: bought and brought to your door

indicators.note: for places the request after the armour, as an order for mail

parts.note: mail is chain armour made of linked rings
an order is a request for goods

explanation.surface: A knight sends off for a suit of armour and has it delivered to his house.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Request for armour' as an ORDER for MAIL, so MAIL comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods purchased by post or catalogue are delivered to the buyer's home address.

clue.text: Trim our size to conform to a beauty product

indicators.note: the letters are made to conform to a new shape, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to slim down to fit an ideal of beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to conform to' rearranges TRIM OUR SIZE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream applied to keep the skin soft and hydrated.

clue.text: Salad stuff put about twice on ship

parts.note: c (circa) is Latin for about, and re also means about or concerning
c (circa) is Latin for about, and re also means about or concerning
SS is short for steamship

explanation.surface: Some greenery is handed round on board a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about twice' asks for two different words for 'about': C (circa) and RE. They go on SS, the abbreviation for steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: This peppery leaf is a common ingredient in sandwiches and green salads.

clue.text: Hurried to suppress amateur measure with bases spread out

indicators.note: to suppress means to hold something inside

parts.note: sped means hurried
lay means non-professional or amateur
a foot is a measure of length

explanation.surface: Someone rushed to stop an amateur measuring with a spread base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to suppress' signals the container: the hurrying word holds the other two. 'bases' looks architectural but means feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Having feet that are turned outwards, so the base of each leg points away.

clue.text: Some think yellow's black 28

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few people reckon a yellow colour is actually dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' shows that the answer sits inside thINK Yellow's.
explanation.definitionFit: Something as dark as printing fluid is deep black in colour.

clue.text: Cut Handel's speciality and name in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: cut tells us to lop the final letter off the composer's form

parts.note: Handel is famed for oratorios such as Messiah
Cal is a man's name, short for Calvin

explanation.surface: An editor trims Handel's best-known form and adds a name in an odd turn of phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' signals losing the final letter of Handel's form. Cal is a short form of names like Calvin.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the style of public speech, pertaining to rhetoric and declamation.

clue.text: Person producing threefold increase, about 1000, is a shaky type

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: one who trebles something is a trebler
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone who triples a sum by about a thousand turns out to be nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets TREBLER around M (Roman 1000).
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something that quivers or shakes, like a nervous person or a vibrating device.

clue.text: From which you could see horse with colic and sign of pain?

parts.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse
wind is gas in the stomach that causes colic
ow is an exclamation of pain

explanation.surface: A vet sees a horse with stomach pain crying out.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole idea of a window: a place from which you could look out.
explanation.definitionFit: A projecting window in a house wall gives a wide view outwards.

clue.text: Silly mimicry in place of primates?

definitions.meaning: foolish copying of others' behaviour, as monkeys copy
read like rookery or piggery, a place where apes are kept

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense coins a word on the pattern of rookery or piggery, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the ape: foolish imitation of others, and a jokey coinage for a home for simians.

clue.text: Sequence of notes about experimental building that can be surmounted

indicators.note: about means the musical sequence goes around the building

parts.note: a scale is a run of notes in order
a lab is a building for experiments

explanation.surface: A run of musical notes around a laboratory that can be climbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container; 'experimental building' is a cryptic way of saying laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be climbed over or ascended can be surmounted.

clue.text: Prepared to understand something unknown

parts.note: to read a situation is to understand it
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: Getting set to grasp a mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: In algebra x, y and z stand for unknown quantities.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ready means being set and equipped for action.

clue.text: A fellow's mythical story, very pleasant

parts.note: F is short for fellow
a fable is a legendary tale

explanation.surface: A fellow has a fairy tale, very cheery.
explanation.walkthrough: F is short for 'fellow', as in FRS (Fellow of the Royal Society).
explanation.definitionFit: A friendly, good-natured and easy-going person is very pleasant company.

clue.text: Cornea is fixed in this plan

indicators.note: fixed in the sense of fiddled or rearranged, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An eye surgeon describes the operation in which the cornea is repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' reshuffles CORNEA plus IS.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline of a possible sequence of events, as in a planner's projected outcome.

clue.text: Give further demonstration and tell off

definitions.meaning: to show again, to prove once more

explanation.definitionFit: Read as re-prove it means to prove again; as one word it means to scold or rebuke someone.

clue.text: Awful barney just in the vicinity

indicators.note: awful suggests these letters have been messed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A terrible quarrel close at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'barney' is British slang for a noisy quarrel; 'Awful' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Close at hand, not far away.

clue.text: Fill frieze depicting film director

indicators.note: depicting suggests the letters are redrawn in a new form

explanation.surface: An instruction to decorate a frieze with a scene of a famous filmmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depicting' rearranges FILL FRIEZE. Franco Zeffirelli was an Italian director of films and operas.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian made films such as Romeo and Juliet (1968).

clue.text: Hits back in argument

indicators.note: back says the word is read from the end to the start

parts.note: taps are light hits

explanation.surface: A boxer strikes back during a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TAPS round; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A petty quarrel or squabble.

clue.text: Old queen's article, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is spoken rather than written

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A former monarch's possession is spoken of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' makes AN sound like the royal name. Queen Anne reigned in Britain from 1702 to 1714.
explanation.definitionFit: The last Stuart monarch, who reigned over Great Britain until 1714.

clue.text: Another attempt to secure contract upset bride

indicators.note: an upset bride is thrown into disorder, so her letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A distressed bride tries once more to get a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges BRIDE. In bridge, a contract is won through bidding.
explanation.definitionFit: A second offer in an auction or in bridge bidding.

clue.text: Take money from popular admiral? He'd give it to the poor

definitions.text: He'd give it to the poor

parts.note: to rob someone is to take their money
in means fashionable or popular
Samuel Hood was a famous British admiral

explanation.surface: A wealthy naval officer is robbed for charity.
explanation.walkthrough: Admiral Hood was a famous British naval commander; the legendary outlaw of Sherwood stole from the rich for the poor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sherwood Forest outlaw of English legend stole from the rich to help the needy.

clue.text: Soundly observe method which ship can use

indicators.note: soundly signals that the word is taken by how it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: to see something is to observe it
a way is a method

explanation.surface: A sound approach to watching how boats travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' is the homophone signal, applying only to the word for observe.
explanation.definitionFit: A navigable inland channel or route for oceangoing vessels.

clue.text: Small opening for viewer to lease

parts.note: an eye is the organ of sight, a viewer
to let is to lease out

explanation.surface: A small gap through which a viewer can rent.
explanation.walkthrough: To LET is the British term for renting out property.
explanation.definitionFit: A small reinforced hole for a lace or cord to pass through.
